title: TemporalGUI: Grounding Temporal and Sequential Instructions in Dynamic GUI States
description:
Problem: Current GUI grounding benchmarks (ScreenSpot, OSWorld-G) treat grounding as a static, single-step mapping from instruction to UI element. Real computer-use tasks often involve multi-step sequential dependencies where the correct grounding target for step N depends on the outcomes of steps N-1 (e.g., 'Click the button that appeared after you opened the dropdown'). Existing datasets and models lack temporal reasoning over evolving GUI states.

Proposed Method: We construct TemporalGUI, a benchmark and training dataset capturing sequential GUI grounding across state transitions. Using automated trajectory recording on web and desktop environments, we extract (initial_state, action_sequence, target_state, instruction) tuples where instructions reference temporally-conditioned elements. We train a grounding model augmented with a lightweight state-diff encoder that highlights changed UI regions between consecutive screenshots, concatenated with the current frame before grounding. We adapt the Jedi synthesis pipeline to generate multi-turn grounding examples by chaining decomposed single-step examples with synthetically injected state transitions.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate static grounding models on TemporalGUI to quantify temporal reasoning gap; (2) Ablate state-diff encoding vs. full screenshot concatenation vs. change captioning; (3) Measure downstream improvement on OSWorld agentic tasks requiring sequential dependencies; (4) Test compositional generalization to unseen application state sequences.

title: GroundingRL: Closing the Loop Between GUI Grounding and Task Completion via Reinforcement Learning from Execution Feedback
description:
Problem: Current GUI grounding models (e.g., Jedi-trained models) are trained via supervised imitation on static datasets, creating a disconnect between grounding accuracy and actual task success. A model can correctly identify the 'right' element yet fail if the broader action sequence is misaligned with task semantics, and vice versa. This supervision gap means grounding improvements don't always translate to proportional agentic gains.

Proposed Method: We propose GroundingRL, a reinforcement learning framework that treats GUI grounding as a sequential decision process and uses execution outcomes as reward signals. Starting from a Jedi-pretrained grounding model, we apply GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) with three reward tiers: (1) binary task completion reward from OSWorld's automated evaluators, (2) intermediate sub-task progress rewards derived from UI state differencing, and (3) a lightweight grounding-consistency reward comparing predicted click coordinates against ground-truth annotations when available. A curriculum scheduler progressively introduces harder tasks as grounding accuracy improves.

Experiments: (1) Compare GroundingRL vs. supervised-only baseline on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena, and OSWorld-G; (2) Ablate each reward component; (3) Analyze how RL fine-tuning shifts the grounding distribution toward task-critical interface regions; (4) Evaluate generalization to unseen applications. We expect >35% success on OSWorld, demonstrating that execution feedback substantially closes the grounding-to-completion gap.

title: TemporalGUI: Grounding Sequential Multi-Step Instructions Across Dynamic Interface States
description:
Problem: Current GUI grounding benchmarks like OSWorld-G and ScreenSpot treat grounding as stateless single-instruction mapping, ignoring that real computer-use tasks require grounding instructions that span multiple interface states (e.g., 'after opening the dropdown, select the third option that appeared'). Agents must resolve referring expressions that depend on prior actions and intermediate UI states, a capability entirely absent from existing datasets and models.

Proposed Method: We construct TemporalGUI, a benchmark and training dataset of multi-step grounding chains where each grounding target is conditioned on a sequence of preceding screenshots and actions. We introduce a state-conditioned grounding model that encodes interface history via a lightweight temporal transformer over screenshot embeddings, concatenated with current-state visual features before predicting target coordinates. We synthesize training data by replaying recorded task demonstrations from OSWorld and AITW, extracting (history, current-screen, instruction) triplets where the correct element is ambiguous without prior context.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate state-of-the-art grounding models on TemporalGUI to quantify the temporal grounding gap. (2) Compare our history-conditioned model against stateless baselines across 1-5 step history lengths. (3) Ablate history encoding strategies (concatenation vs. cross-attention vs. state summarization). (4) Integrate temporal grounding into an OSWorld agent and measure task completion improvements on multi-step tasks requiring state-dependent element selection.

title: GroundingRL: Closing the Loop Between GUI Grounding Accuracy and Agent Task Success via Reinforcement Learning from Execution Feedback
description: Problem: While Jedi demonstrates that better grounding improves agentic task completion (5%→27% on OSWorld), grounding models are still trained with supervised objectives on static datasets, creating a disconnect between grounding accuracy metrics and downstream task success. A grounding model that scores well on ScreenSpot may still fail at critical action steps that determine task outcomes. Proposed Method: We introduce GroundingRL, a reinforcement learning framework that fine-tunes GUI grounding models using sparse execution feedback from a live environment. Rather than supervising each click/action independently, we use task-level binary rewards (task succeeded/failed) and credit-assign them back to individual grounding decisions via a lightweight advantage estimation over the action trajectory. We augment this with a dense reward signal derived from intermediate environment state changes (e.g., correct UI element changed state), reducing reward sparsity. We additionally propose a curriculum that starts with single-step grounding tasks and progressively introduces multi-step dependencies. Experiments: We evaluate on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena, comparing against Jedi-trained supervised models, showing task completion rate, grounding precision at critical steps, and sample efficiency. Ablations examine reward shaping strategies, curriculum design, and whether RL generalizes grounding to unseen applications beyond the training distribution.

title: TemporalGUI: Grounding GUI Actions Across Dynamic Interface State Transitions
description: Problem: Current GUI grounding benchmarks like OSWorld-G treat grounding as a static, single-frame mapping problem. Models trained on static snapshots fail to ground actions conditioned on expected post-interaction states or multi-step context. Proposed Method: We construct TemporalGUI, a dataset of 500K+ multi-frame GUI grounding examples captured as (context_frames, instruction, target_frame, action) tuples, synthesized by replaying interaction traces from web and desktop applications and recording full state transitions. We augment the Jedi synthesis pipeline with a temporal perturbation module that generates counterfactual interface states (e.g., dropdown open/closed, form filled/empty) to train models to ground actions conditioned on anticipated state changes. We propose a dual-encoder architecture with a temporal difference module that attends to regions of predicted UI change, trained with a contrastive objective between pre/post-action frames. Experiments: We evaluate on a new TemporalGUI benchmark requiring state-conditional grounding, test on OSWorld full task completion (building on the 5%→27% result), and ablate the value of temporal context versus single-frame baselines, showing compositional generalization to unseen application state combinations.

title: TemporalGUI: Grounding Sequential Multi-Step Instructions Across Dynamic Interface State Transitions
description:

Experiments: (1) Benchmark existing grounding models on TemporalGUI to quantify the temporal dependency gap; (2) Ablate state-delta encoding vs. naive frame stacking vs. history summarization; (3) Measure downstream agentic performance on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena, comparing sequential grounding accuracy and task completion rates against Jedi-trained baselines.

title: TemporalGrounding: Benchmarking and Training GUI Agents for Dynamic Interface States Across Time
description:

We extend the Jedi synthesis pipeline to generate temporally-conditioned training pairs by: (1) recording before/after screenshot pairs during automated UI interactions, (2) synthesizing instructions that explicitly reference delta states using a VLM, and (3) training a dual-encoder grounding model that conditions on both current and previous frames via a lightweight temporal attention module appended to the Jedi architecture.

Experiments: Evaluate on TemporalGrounding-Bench (primary), OSWorld-G and ScreenSpot-v2 (regression). Ablate single-frame vs. multi-frame conditioning, temporal attention depth, and number of historical frames (1-5). Measure downstream agent performance on OSWorld tasks requiring multi-step form filling and dynamic content interaction, expecting 10-15% improvement over static grounding baselines.

title: GroundingRL: Closing the Loop Between GUI Grounding and Task Reward via Reinforcement Learning from Execution Feedback
description: Problem: Current GUI grounding models like Jedi are trained via supervised imitation on static datasets, creating a distribution gap between grounding accuracy on benchmarks and actual task success in dynamic environments. At each agent step, the grounding model proposes a target element and confidence; the action is executed in a sandboxed OS environment (OSWorld), and task progress signals (partial completion, error recovery, goal achievement) are converted into dense reward. We apply GRPO with a composite reward: (1) binary execution success, (2) UI state change consistency, and (3) a lightweight critic scoring semantic alignment between instruction and observed post-action state. The grounding model thus learns which ambiguous phrasings reliably map to correct elements under real interaction dynamics. Experiments: We compare against Jedi supervised baseline and GPT-4o on OSWorld full benchmark, measuring task success rate, grounding accuracy on OSWorld-G, and generalization to novel application domains not seen during RL training. We categorize temporal grounding into: (1) state-relative references ('the button that was previously disabled'), (2) history-dependent targets ('the file you just opened'), and (3) delta-conditioned manipulation ('increase the value you decreased earlier'). We train a time-aware grounding model incorporating a lightweight state-change encoder that attends over compressed frame differences alongside standard visual tokens.

Experiments: We evaluate on 400 curated temporal grounding samples, comparing static Jedi-trained models vs. our temporal extension. We measure grounding accuracy stratified by temporal depth (1-5 prior states) and demonstrate downstream improvement on OSWorld sequential task completion, targeting 15+ percentage point gains over static grounding baselines.

title: TemporalGUI: Grounding Dynamic Interface States Through Time-Aware Decomposition
description: Problem: Current GUI grounding benchmarks like OSWorld-G and ScreenSpot treat interfaces as static snapshots, ignoring that real-world computer use involves temporally evolving UI states where element appearance, position, and availability change based on prior actions (e.g., dropdown menus appearing after clicks, modal dialogs blocking content, form validation changing button states). Models trained on static decompositions like Jedi fail to ground instructions referencing transient or context-dependent UI states. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalGUI, a benchmark and training framework that explicitly models UI state transitions. We record multi-step interaction trajectories and annotate grounding targets at each timestep, labeling elements by their temporal availability (persistent/transient/conditional). We synthesize a temporal grounding dataset by augmenting Jedi-style decomposition with before/after screenshot pairs and delta-state descriptions, training a grounding model with a lightweight temporal attention module that conditions on previous UI state embeddings alongside the current screenshot. We also introduce 'negative grounding' examples where the target element is absent due to wrong temporal context. Experiments: We evaluate on a new TemporalGUI benchmark (300 multi-step trajectories, 1500 timestep-grounding pairs), ScreenSpot-v2, and OSWorld, measuring grounding accuracy on transient vs. persistent elements separately and downstream task completion improvement on time-sensitive workflows like form filling and multi-dialog navigation.

title: TemporalGUI: Grounding Sequential Multi-Step Instructions Across Dynamic Interface States
description:
Problem: Current GUI grounding benchmarks (including OSWorld-G) treat grounding as single-turn, static snapshots — mapping one instruction to one UI element. Real computer tasks require grounding sequences of instructions across dynamically changing interface states, where each action transforms the UI and context for subsequent steps. Existing models and datasets fundamentally lack temporal, multi-step grounding capability.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalGUI, a framework for sequential grounding that (1) constructs a new benchmark of 800+ multi-step task traces where each step's grounding depends on prior action outcomes and evolving UI state, capturing phenomena like form filling, wizard navigation, and conditional branching; (2) synthesizes a 1M-example sequential grounding dataset by augmenting Jedi-style decomposition with state-transition graphs — encoding before/after screenshot pairs, instruction chains, and action dependencies; (3) trains a grounding model with a lightweight state-tracking module (cross-attention over previous screenshot-action pairs) prepended to a vision-language backbone, enabling contextual grounding without full agent-loop inference.

Experiments: We benchmark against single-step grounding models (including Jedi-trained models) on our sequential benchmark, ablate state history length, evaluate on OSWorld end-to-end agent tasks, and measure compositional generalization to unseen application sequences. We expect 15-20% improvement over stateless baselines on multi-step grounding accuracy.
